title: Lawsuit alleges RCMP misconduct in death of Whistler business owner
subtitle: "Jason Koehler's last words to RCMP were, 'Don't kill me,'" the document reads.
article: A notice of civil claim filed this week in B.C. Supreme Court in Kamloops alleges police in Whistler acted with "extreme and excessive use of force" during a March incident that left a man dead.
Jason Koehler died on March 8 following an altercation with a number of Whistler RCMP officers at a restaurant in the resort community.
Koehler's family is suing the four police officers at the scene when he died. The lawsuit was filed in Kamloops as one of the lawyers representing the plaintiffs is with Jensen Law Group.
Koehler, a Whistler business owner, had mental-health issues, which led to police being called to the restaurant.

In the notice of claim, Koehler's family alleges four Mounties made no attempt to de-escalate the situation with Koehler before turning violent.

"The initial three RCMP members, John Doe 1 to 3, arrived on the scene at the restaurant and resorted to the use of physical force shortly after arriving, including using a Taser on Jason Koehler, with limited efforts to de-escalating the situation and no reason to believe bodily harm to anyone was imminent," the document states.

"John Doe officer 4 arrived on the scene, escalated the situation and, along with the other RCMP members, used excessive force. John Doe officer 4, in addition to using excessive force, acted in an intentional or extremely reckless manner, making a poorly handled situation substantially worse by acting with malice or gross negligence in his extreme and excessive use of force."
The notice of claim describes Koehler as unarmed and non-violent, raising his hands above his head.
"Jason Koehler's last words to RCMP were, 'Don't kill me,'" the document reads.

"Jason Koehler was Tasered, pepper sprayed and beaten with batons by the four RCMP members, including John Doe officer 4, to the point that he lost consciousness on the scene and could not be revived," the document reads.

The notice of claim alleges police used force on Koehler "specifically intended to inflict emotional distress. The RCMP members continued to use force long after it should have been clear that such force was unnecessary."
The family is seeking money to cover funeral expenses, loss of support, loss of household services, loss of inheritance and travel costs, as well as aggravated damages and punitive damages.
The four Mounties, as well as Canada's attorney general and B.C.'s public-safety minister, have 21 days to respond once they are served.
None of the allegations in the claim have been proven in court.
